title: Aztec Gods and Human Sacrifices
subtitle: Blood for the sun
subject: mythologie
description: Among the Aztecs, the sun only rises if the gods receive blood. A harsh, but coherent, cosmology at the heart of their empire.

hero.hook: Without blood, the sun would stop: such is the cosmic debt of the Aztecs.

blocks.text: The **Aztecs**, or Mexica, believe that the universe is fragile. The gods need blood for the sun to continue its course. Without offerings, chaos would return.
What horrified the Spaniards is based on a clear idea: the lives of gods and men are linked. Here's how this cosmology works.

sections.title: The Five Suns: a world already dead four times

blocks.text: According to the  myth, four eras have already disappeared in catastrophes. We are experiencing the fifth sun,  (“4-Movement”), promised to end with earthquakes. [[Five Suns]] [[Nahui Ollin]]

blocks.caption: Stone of the Sun: Aztec time turns into successive eras.

blocks.text: In **Teotihuacán**, a sacred city on the central plateau, the gods throw themselves into a fire to become sun and moon. But the sun remains still. The other gods then offer their own blood to set it in motion. Men inherit this debt.
For the Aztecs, sacrifice is not gratuitous cruelty: it is the repayment of a divine debt, the . [[Cosmology of the Five Suns and cosmic debt]]

The central god is , god of war and the midday sun. Every night, he fights the darkness to be reborn in the morning. At his side,  gives rain, therefore crops, or famine. [[Huitzilopochtli, the sun god]] [[Tlaloc]]

blocks.caption: Huitzilopochtli, warrior sun who demands to be nourished.

blocks.text: , the Feathered Serpent, embodies knowledge and civilization. His rival , the Smoking Mirror, rules the night, destiny and magic. The earth itself has a terrible face: , devouring mother goddess. [[Quetzalcoatl]] [[Tezcatlipoca]] [[Coatlicue]]
The precious blood offered to the gods is called , “precious water”. The extracted heart is thought of as a solar spark returned to the sky. [[chalchihuatl]]
To obtain victims, the Aztecs organize the , the “flower wars”: ritual combats whose goal is not to kill, but to capture living warriors worthy of being offered. [[Xochiyaoyotl]]

blocks.caption: Sacrifice at the top of the temple: the heart presented to the sun.

blocks.text: At the top of the **Templo Mayor** in Tenochtitlán, the lakeside capital, a priest extracts the heart with a knife from **Obsidian**, a sharp volcanic stone. The gesture is public, solemn, thought of as a service rendered to the sun.

events.title: Sacrifice of the gods
events.detail: The sun receives divine blood to move forward.

sections.title: End of a world, lasting traces

blocks.text: Spanish chronicles sometimes inflate the figures to justify the conquest. But the sacrificial system is very real. In **1519**, the arrival of **Hernán Cortés** precipitates the end of this ritual universe.

However, Aztec figures survive in syncretism: the Virgin of Guadalupe appears on a site once linked to a mother goddess. To understand these sacrifices is to understand a culture that places the survival of the cosmos above the individual.
Among the Aztecs, human blood nourished the sun. The gods have already paid with their lives: men repay this debt through sacrifice, notably via **flower wars**.
